cohort: The study included 51,225 singleton deliveries to women aged 20 years or older with a gestational age of at least 22 weeks, occurring between 2004 and 2012 in a London maternity unit.
finding: Increasing maternal age from 25 was associated with a gradual increase in the risk of caesarean delivery and postpartum haemorrhage, while women over 35 had an elevated risk of low birthweight and preterm birth.
mod_finding: Increasing maternal age was associated with an increase in caesarean delivery, particularly elective caesareans, with a higher prevalence observed in older nulliparous women.
